name: UCDoor compatibility wrapper

mappings.rationale: The UCDoor SDK documents cd_PutStr as its callable terminal string-output operation.
The UCDoor SDK provides string and prompted-string terminal input calls.
limitations: The extracted evidence does not fully normalize editing behavior, maximum-length handling, or disconnect signaling.

evidence.note: The header defines selector 7 as minutes online left.
The original demo retrieves and displays current time left.

mappings.rationale: cd_GetNumInfo with UDC_TIMELEFT returns the remaining online time.
limitations: UCDoor reports minutes while the canonical ODS result is seconds, so an adapter must convert units.

evidence.note: The guide documents carrier-loss detection followed by cd_End(ERROR_CARRIER).
The original demo returns the carrier error after cd_CarrierLost reports true.

mappings.rationale: The SDK explicitly documents detecting carrier loss and ending with the carrier-loss reason.

evidence.note: The SDK documents cd_GetChar as returning one character entered by the user.
The prompted variant displays a supplied prompt and returns one character.
The original SDK demo reads and displays a caller-entered character.

mappings.rationale: The SDK provides callable single-character terminal input with optional prompting.

evidence.note: The public header defines the current-user name selector for cd_GetStrInfo.
The guide documents string-info retrieval and stable user-index lookup by name.
The original SDK demo retrieves and displays the current caller's username.

mappings.rationale: UCDoor exposes the current caller's username and a documented lookup for its stable user index.

evidence.note: The SDK defines this call as performing a function from the MAX menu configuration.
The HTML reference preserves the function signature and example invocation.
The public header declares the function, extra argument, and string parameters.

mappings.rationale: cd_DoFunction directly invokes a numbered MAX menu-configured function from the door.

evidence.note: The guide defines cd_Main as the lifecycle entry point, calls user code through cd_Door, and reports OK when the door ends normally.
The HTML reference identifies OK as the normal door-completion result.
The original demo returns from its cd_Door callback to the cd_Main lifecycle wrapper.

mappings.rationale: Returning from cd_Door through cd_Main is the SDK-documented normal completion path back to the host.

limitations: Only operations directly documented by the cataloged SDK are reviewed; no canonical status.set operation is established.
